mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.25% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1 standard deviation within the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >1 SD in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by more than one standard deviation in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) and real personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a shift from saving to investment, which boosts economic activity and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12MA and RSAFS > 12MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.5% signals an unexpected surge in inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following a monthly CPIAUCSL increase above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic recession, which reliably predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline.
